The image shows soybean stems split open revealing:
- White/bleached internal pith tissue
- Black sclerotia (hard, dark structures) embedded within the white tissue
- Bleached exterior stem appearance

This strongly suggests **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot). Let me confirm with the reference image.

The reference confirms White Mold characteristics. The test image shows mature/late-season White Mold with:
- Bleached white stems split open
- Black sclerotia (hard, dark oval structures) embedded throughout the white pith — the hallmark diagnostic feature
- Completely bleached/whitened stem tissue

The reference shows earlier-stage fluffy mycelial growth, but the test image represents the classic late-season presentation where stems are bleached white with black sclerotia clearly visible inside — perfectly matching the symptom description: "hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems."
